reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let I be any finite index type. Let V:E->R be C^2 and let kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa. Suppose that, for every x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon such that 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0, a real h>=0, and arbitrary deterministic arrays t:I->R, omega:I x I->R, b:I->R, and d:I->R. Here b and d denote positionWeight and momentumWeight.
Then there exist measurable maps p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
The finite exact-real interpreter run(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) fails with none when fuel is zero. With positive fuel it sets next=y-eta g(x). If ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon it returns (x,1); otherwise it recurses from next with one less unit of fuel and adds one to the successful query count. Thus the displayed equality supplies a finite successful run starting at y, using fuel N(y)+1, with output q(y) and reported count exactly N(y)+1.
For these witnesses put a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), and let gamma be the product law of mutually independent standard Gaussian E-valued variables u,v,(xi_j)_{j in I},(xi'_j)_{j in I}; explicitly gamma=(G x G) x ((product_I G) x (product_I G)), where G is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. For an incoming state s=(x,r) in E x E and a noise sample z=((u,v),(xi,xi')), define
  P0=a r+sigma u,
  Y0_i=x+t_i P0,
  Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta) xi_j),
  Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_{j in I} omega_{ij} Z0_j,
  Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta) xi'_j),
  Phi(s,z)=(x+h P0-sum_{j in I} b_j Z1_j,
            a(P0-sum_{j in I} d_j Z1_j)+sigma v).
Then 1-exp(-h)>=0, Phi is jointly measurable on (E x E) x ((E x E) x ((I->E) x (I->E))), and there exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E satisfying, for every s,
  K(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma.
Equivalently, for every Borel output event A, K(s,A)=gamma({z:Phi(s,z) in A}); each K(s) is a probability measure and its value on each measurable event depends measurably on s. All sums use the entire finite index type. This statement asserts the existence and measurability of these witnesses and transition kernel; it gives no invariant-distribution, convergence, bias, or uniform query-complexity conclusion.
objects: The potential V, Hessian quadratic form D^2 V(x)[v,v], real inner-product gradient grad V, parameters kappa/eta/c/epsilon/h, deterministic finite arrays t/omega/positionWeight/momentumWeight, measurable proximal-solution witness p, measurable approximate-solution witness q, measurable natural-valued witness N, the finite exact-real interpreter run, standard Gaussian measure G, product noise law gamma, joint state/noise map Phi, and probability-valued Markov kernel K. The incoming state is (position x, momentum r); noise consists of u,v and two independent finite E-valued arrays xi and xi-prime.
domains: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, CompleteSpace, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. I is an arbitrary Fintype, including possibly an empty type. V:E->R; kappa is in the nonnegative reals; eta,c,epsilon,h are real. t,positionWeight,momentumWeight:I->R and omega:I->I->R. p,q:E->E and N:E->N. gamma is a probability measure on (E x E) x ((I->E) x (I->E)). Phi maps (E x E) x ((E x E) x ((I->E) x (I->E))) to E x E. K has incoming and outgoing state space E x E.
quantifiers: Universally quantified: admissible spaces E and finite I; V and kappa satisfying the stated conditions; eta,c,epsilon satisfying their inequalities; every real h>=0; and arbitrary deterministic arrays t,omega,positionWeight,momentumWeight. Existentially, after these fixed data, there are p,q,N satisfying global measurability and the three simultaneous pointwise conditions for every y in E. With those witnesses used to define Phi, there exists a Markov kernel K whose measure equality holds for every incoming state s in E x E. The Hessian inequalities are universal in both x and v in E. No existential choice is made separately for each y or each incoming state.
assumptions: 1<=kappa with kappa nonnegative; V is C^2 over R; for every x,v, kappa^(-1)||v||^2<=D^2 V(x)[v,v]<=||v||^2; 0<eta, eta<=c, c<1; epsilon>0; h>=0. The space and finite-index structures are as stated in domains. The arrays are arbitrary real-valued deterministic functions, without positivity, normalization, consistency, order, or stability hypotheses. Standard Gaussian means centered identity-covariance Gaussian, and gamma is the independent product of the specified Gaussian measures. run uses exact real arithmetic and the specified residual stopping test.
conclusion: There are measurable global p,q,N with p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon, and a successful run starting at y with fuel and reported query count N(y)+1 and returned point q(y), for every y. For a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), and the explicitly reconstructed two-stage finite gradient map Phi, the variance expression 1-exp(-h) is nonnegative, Phi is jointly measurable, and its gamma pushforward at each incoming state defines a Markov kernel K. The gradient probes use q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)xi_j and q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta)xi-prime_j. The outgoing position uses the second-stage probes and h P0; the outgoing momentum is a times P0 minus the momentum-weighted second-stage sum, followed by the additive noise sigma v.
scopes: The witnesses p,q,N apply to all y in E at once. Their run/error condition concerns the implicit equation at each input y, rather than a final transition error estimate. Phi is jointly measurable in the incoming state and every noise coordinate; the kernel equality concerns the full output probability measure for every incoming state. The two noise arrays and the two scalar-stage Gaussian vectors are independent under gamma, although outputs and internal stages need not be independent. Finite sums range over all I. The interpreter equality records the successful final iterate and its exact reported count; no uniform-in-y bound on N is asserted. No stationarity, invariance, convergence, numerical-bias bound, or comparison to another transition is asserted.
constant_dependencies: All data E,I,V,kappa,eta,c,epsilon,h,t,omega,positionWeight,momentumWeight are fixed before the existential witnesses, so the theorem syntax permits p,q,N and K to depend on those fixed data; it does not specify uniqueness or a reduced dependence set for the witnesses. The explicit coefficients a and sigma depend only on h, while sqrt(eta) depends on eta. The Gaussian law depends on E and I. The stopping threshold is (1-eta)epsilon. c bounds eta and does not occur in the conclusion formulas; kappa enters the hypotheses but not the displayed transition formula. No numerical constant or global query-complexity bound is supplied.
